summary: An excerpt from a fiction book (Book 4, part 41) in which Anda, a teenage gamer, returns to an online game after almost a month locked out of her PC by her dad. She reunites with her squad leader Sarge, who has been worried about her. They plan four missions using the BFG10K, and Anda raises a union organizer named Raymond and the exploitation of the 'noobs' in the cottages, which Lucy questions.
one_line: Anda returns to an online war game after a month locked out of her PC, and debates labor exploitation of 'noobs' with Lucy and Sarge.
key_facts: Anda has been locked out of her PC for almost a month, kept under lock-and-key in her dad's study.
Anda has been on medications with no telly and no gaming, and attends double PE periods at school with the other whales.
Anda eats sweeties and drinks fizzy drink in the park after trips to the newsagents at the 501-meter mark.
Anda is back at the PC Baang, a place described as filled with stinky, loud, obnoxious spotty boys who smell like goats.
Sarge tells Anda she was getting worried about her and that she should have found a way to let her know.
Sarge has a backlog of missions and says Anda is too good to replace, having tried going out with a couple of other girls.
Sarge proposes four missions for the day, using the BFG10K.
One BFG10K bolt is made up of 20 regular BFG bolts, each costing a small fortune in gold.
The team started with five BFG10K bolts and used them all on the first three targets.
After returning the BFG10K to the armory, they grabbed a couple of BFGs before setting out for the fourth target.
Anda met a noob in the cottage after the last campaign, who said he was a union organizer named Raymond.
Sarge says she met Raymond too, that he has been turning up everywhere, and calls him a creep.
Sarge asks Anda whether she is fine with depriving little kids of their wages.
Lucy's voice becomes brittle when she addresses Anda about the noobs' wages.
